A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KineMask and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Their shared experiments and reorganized material can be reliably matched despite the format change.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data experiments, ablations, a 30-participant user study, qualitative evaluations, and appendix comparisons using CogVideoX and Wan backbones.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Cosmos evaluations, additional backbone user-study results, and qualitative hand-object and hand-tool-object demonstrations.

M1.justification: The two-stage ControlNet procedure, velocity-mask encoding, mask dropout, objectives, and SAM2/GPT-5 inference pipeline remain unchanged. Applying KineMask to additional backbones does not introduce a documented change to its algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds qualitative hand-object and hand-tool-object scenarios in Figures 8 and 18. This is a limited extension of interaction coverage; the Simple Motion, Interactions, and Real World evaluation framework remains.

E2.justification: Cosmos becomes an evaluated comparator in Table 4 and Figure 10. The original comparator set remains represented, including PhysGen3D. Wan was already evaluated in v2's appendix, while the newly cited Goal Force is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds the Cosmos2.5-2B configuration and a user study comparing KineMask-Wan and KineMask-Cosmos with their respective backbones using the existing three-axis protocol. Retained dataset splits, metrics, generation length, and stated training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds hand-interaction generalization case studies and extends the backbone analysis. It removes v2 Figure 12's direct comparison illustrating Wan-specific failures relative to KineMask-CogVideoX. The training-stage, data, caption, velocity-encoding, and dropout ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and user-preference percentages without seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional study does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice or an explicit increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 substantially expands the evidence with Cosmos results, additional backbone preference results, and hand-interaction demonstrations. Table 4 adds Cosmos baseline/KineMask FVD values of 1287.3/433.6. Figure 10 adds motion/interaction/physical preference rates of 71/70/70% for KineMask-Wan and 70/60/56% for KineMask-Cosmos. Tables 1–3 and 5, existing Table 4 rows, and the original user-study percentages remain unchanged. These are added comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same definitions and objectives. Neither version adds theorems, proofs, formal assumptions, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v3's abstract explicitly claims hand-object generalization, and its introduction and conclusion emphasize applicability across multiple VDMs. These broaden the stated contributions while retaining the original claims about two-stage motion conditioning and realistic rigid-body interactions.

C2.justification: v3 explains hand-interaction transfer through learned collision behavior combined with pretrained knowledge, and emphasizes the role of backbone physical priors. It omits v2's specific rationale for preferring CogVideoX over Wan. The physical-control limitations and general failure-mode discussion remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B and nvidia/Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B checkpoint identifiers and identifies Unsplash as an image source. It removes v2's instructions for opening the supplementary-video website, without establishing that the resource was withdrawn. Existing training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Goal Force to the physics-aware related-work discussion and adds an Unsplash reference. The main novelty positioning and the remaining cited research are retained.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized revisions to the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Related work gains numbered subsections, backbone generalization receives main-text treatment, the appendix is reorganized, and the author list changes. The writing-assistance disclosure is omitted.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. v3 adds generalization and backbone-comparison displays, expands Table 4, rearranges qualitative panels, and removes v2's full synthetic-video/mask montage and direct backbone-failure panel. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The Cosmos evaluation and additional backbone user study strengthen evidence for generality beyond the Wan results already present in v2. Hand-interaction examples add limited qualitative support. These benefits outweigh the loss of the explicit Wan failure comparison and supplementary-video access instructions, but the unchanged central method and existing validation make the overall improvement limited.
